sources.title: M.Ahmed, Survey of Traditional Crafts, Census of India1961, VolXII PartVII-A, Orissa
sources.publication: Printed1967; Census1961series is not exact publicationdate
sources.status: Original officialPDF downloaded and relevant chapters read
claims: Kantilo survey reports249workshops and1103workers;912were Kansari, including90women. Other communities also worked in the industry: occupational participation did not imply caste identity.
Family workshops trained boys by observation and progressively harder tasks. The account describes cooperatives helping procure raw metals and production interrupted by supply shortages.

Tarbha chapter recounts Kansari families moving from bell-metal work into silversmithy, learning from existing smiths and teaching relatives. It explicitly identifies the family of Paramanand Sahu; attribution comes from survey account, not surname.

The earlier family migration is narrated as roughly200–250years before the survey without a cited dated charter. Do not calculate a settled arrivaldate or treat a local family story as origin of the whole community.
limits: Keep entire volume within one200wordderivedbudget; do not split chapters merely to multiply budget.
TableOCR has inconsistent Thodia numbers; use verified aggregate figures or avoid counts. Table present-position year OCR1864 likely1964 but unverified visually; omit thatdate.
Historical district names preserved; Kantilo then-Puri is not current district claim.
Do not adopt stereotyped praise, castehierarchy or dismissive descriptions of customers.
